description:
Storage owns a read that returns exactly the records one checkout's store holds — its issue
records and its event log — with no aggregation from version-control history or another
checkout.

## Background

The ordinary issue and index readers deliberately union the local store, versioned history,
and the primary checkout, which is the documented adopter-facing read model. A divergence
comparison needs the opposite: the records one store actually holds, because the union masks
exactly the one-sided records such a comparison exists to surface. Persistence access belongs
to the storage layer, so the exact read is a storage-owned operation that a command consumes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A storage-owned read returns exactly the issue records and event records one checkout's store holds, with no fallback to versioned history or another checkout's store.
- [hard] REQ-02: A record held only by a different checkout's store does not appear in the read's result, proven by a test that would fail under the aggregating readers.
- [hard] REQ-03: The read is read-only, and it works against a checkout store other than the one the process runs in.
- [hard] REQ-04: The existing aggregated readers keep their documented behaviour unchanged.

## Notes

The exact read is a storage-owned operation addressed at an explicit store location, not a
method on the shared issue-store interface, so the in-memory implementation and its shared
behavioural contract are not engaged.
title: Exact single-store read for cross-checkout comparison
